project: Des Moines AI Pulse — iOS Native App
description: iOS Native App Hardening — Comprehensive audit-driven improvements now fully implemented in the native SwiftUI app (ios/DesMoinesInsider/). Original Capacitor-based mobile-app/ has been removed. All features are native Swift: haptics via UIImpactFeedbackGenerator, pull-to-refresh via .refreshable, LazyVStack virtualization, NavigationStack transitions, NWPathMonitor networking, CachedAsyncImage, and UNUserNotificationCenter for local reminders.

userStories.title: Fix image overflow breaking page layout on iOS
userStories.description: As a mobile user, I need images to never exceed the viewport width so that the page layout stays intact and all buttons/text remain accessible.
acceptanceCriteria: Global CSS reset: img, video { max-width: 100%; height: auto } in @layer base
html.capacitor-app has overflow-x: hidden (not just body/#root)
Capacitor-specific img max-width: 100% !important safety net
All image containers in cards/detail pages have overflow-hidden
No horizontal scroll on any page when viewing wide event/restaurant images
Build passes (npm run build)
userStories.notes: Native SwiftUI: handled by .resizable() + .clipped() on all CachedAsyncImage usages. No viewport overflow possible in native layout.

Call hapticTap() on nav item click instead of navigator.vibrate

userStories.notes: Native SwiftUI: UIImpactFeedbackGenerator used throughout — nav items, favorite toggles, share buttons, filter selections.

userStories.title: Add network status indicator for offline/slow connections

userStories.title: Wire up push notification registration and event reminders

userStories.notes: Native SwiftUI: PushNotificationService registers with APNs, syncs token to Supabase via edge function. LocalNotificationService schedules event reminders via UNCalendarNotificationTrigger (1hr before). Remind Me button in EventDetailView toggles reminders with haptic feedback.

userStories.title: Add iOS-native image viewer for event/restaurant photos

userStories.notes: Native SwiftUI: LazyVStack is SwiftUI's built-in virtualization — only renders visible cells with automatic recycling. No custom implementation needed.

userStories.title: Cache images locally for faster repeat loads
